claims.text: Crystal-structure selection in noble-metal-based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles is governed by the balance between kinetic trapping and atomic homogenization during thermal processing.
Under rapid heating and cooling, differences in elemental surface energies and diffusion rates kinetically trap atoms in segregated or multiphase configurations.
A gradual thermal cycle with an intermediate dwell allows the constituent atoms to equilibrate.
Atomic equilibration during a gradual thermal cycle enables configurational entropy to stabilize a single-phase solid solution.
Noble-metal-based HEA nanoparticles synthesized under rapid heating and cooling display phase separation and elemental segregation.
Noble-metal-based HEA nanoparticles synthesized under rapid heating and cooling display irregular particle morphology.
Slowing the heating rate and adding an intermediate dwell will isolate diffusion kinetics as the main processing variable when composition, atmosphere, and thermal window are held constant.
The constituent metals have different diffusion barriers.
Extended diffusion time redistributes the constituent atoms more uniformly.
Extended diffusion time counteracts kinetic trapping produced by rapid heating and cooling.
Rapid thermal cycles produce diffusion-rate mismatch that causes phase separation and elemental segregation.
Relative to rapid processing, the controlled slower thermal cycle will yield a more homogeneous single-phase crystal structure.
Relative to rapid processing, the controlled slower thermal cycle will reduce atomic-scale elemental segregation.
Relative to rapid processing, the controlled slower thermal cycle will improve particle morphology.
The proposed effect applies to near-equimolar nanoparticles containing at least five noble metals.
The relevant thermal window must activate diffusion without causing decomposition of the single-phase state.
Optimal heating rates, dwell temperatures, and dwell durations for complete homogenization have not been quantitatively determined.
The relative contributions of surface diffusion and bulk diffusion in these nanoparticles remain unresolved.

contradictions.description: The conditions require more than five noble metals, whereas the boundary includes compositions with at least five noble metals; these scopes differ for exactly five-metal systems.

The hypothesis treats longer diffusion time as homogenizing and suppressing segregation, but the cited AuCoCuNiPt evidence reports that pronounced atomic diffusion drives progressive high-temperature phase separation and rules out sluggish diffusion in that system.
